merger_description:
St Vincent's Private Hospitals Limited (the **Acquirer**), a subsidiary of St Vincent's Health Australia Limited (**St Vincent's Health Australia**), proposes to acquire the assets and operations of St Vincent's Private Hospital Sydney (**Hospital**) from the Congregation of the Religious Sisters of Charity of Australia (**Congregation**) and the Trustees of the Sisters of Charity of Australia (**TSCA**) in both its personal capacity and as trustee for the SVPH Sydney Trust (the **Acquisition**).

The Acquirer is a not-for-profit operator of 9 private hospitals in Australia, with facilities in Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland. St Vincent's Health Australia is an incorporated not-for-profit organisation which acts as the parent company for the majority of charitable health and aged care services previously operated by TSCA.

The Hospital is a 310-bed leading medical and surgical hospital located in Darlinghurst, New South Wales, that provides overnight and day-only care across a broad spectrum of specialties, including cardiology, neurosurgery and orthopaedics.

The application arises out of the unique governance structure of the Hospital. While it functions as part of the Acquirer group of hospitals, it is a separate legal entity because of a bequest which requires it to continue to be operated by TSCA and the Congregation.

TSCA and the Congregation are both registered charities with the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission. TSCA is a statutory body corporate formed under the Roman Catholic Church Communities' Lands Act 1942 (NSW).

The Acquisition will not change the operation of the Hospital, nor the other facilities operated by the Acquirer.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There will be no horizontal consolidation, removal of a
competitor, or practical change to the daily management and
operation of the Hospital post-Acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC also considered the potential application of section
51ABD of the Act. However, the applicant submitted there is some
uncertainty as to whether section 51ABD would apply given the
nature of the relationship between the parties. Having regard to the
particular circumstances, including the consequences of non-
notification in reliance on section 51ABD if it was found not to apply,
the ACCC considers it appropriate to make a determination on the
basis that the acquisition provisions in the Act apply to the
Acquisition.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
